title: Route Fabric Latency Chronometer: streaming vs blocking breakdowns
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Goal: Build a cross-cutting latency dashboard (Chronometer) that surfaces end-to-end token and response latency across the route fabric with explicit breakdowns for streaming vs blocking IO modes. This ticket consolidates telemetry (traces, metrics, logs) and implements panels for p50/p95/p99, incremental token latency (first-byte vs per-token delta), tail attribution by component (ingress, routing, runtime queue, model inference, egress), and error-rate overlays. The dashboard will be used by SREs, runtime engineers, and PMs to identify regression windows and triage streaming vs non-streaming degradations.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard deployed in Console under Observability > Latency > Route Fabric Chronometer
Panels for p50/p95/p99 by route and by model are present and queryable for selectable time ranges
Explicit streaming vs blocking toggle that re-queries metrics and shows differential percentiles
Token-level waterfall panel showing first-byte latency and per-token delta for sampled traces
Trace hook integration: sampled traces linked from percentile panels to X-ray trace view (trace-id links)
Error rate and 5xx overlay panel per route with correlated latency spikes
Baseline comparison and regression flagging for the last 7/30d and an automated alerting rule for p99 > threshold
Documentation page (Confluence) with how to interpret panels and recommended triage playbook
work_items: Instrument new streaming hook to emit sample events at start/end of streaming session (ENG-RTE-2026)
Add 'io_mode' tag (streaming|blocking) to all latency metrics and traces where missing
Create PromQL and tracing queries to compute token-delta percentiles and first-byte latency
Design dashboard layout and wireframes with Design (DES-422) and iterate on placement
Implement dashboard panels in Grafana/Console and add filtering by tenant/model/route
Add alert (Ops) for p99 increase correlated with error-rate > 0.5% for 10m
End-to-end QA with synthetic traffic (short/long sequences, streaming chunk sizes)
notes_and_tradeoffs: Sampling: we will sample 1/200 streaming requests for token-level waterfalls to limit egress and storage costs. This may miss some tail events but keeps cost bounded.
Aggregation cadence: compute percentiles on 1m buckets and roll up to 5m for longer windows to balance query cost vs granularity.
Trace linking: we add a lightweight trace-id header to metrics rather than full span export for high-throughput routes to avoid trace sampling explosion.
Privacy/PII: token-level text is not exported. Waterfall uses timing deltas and anonymized token counts only.
Retention: raw sampled token deltas retained for 30d; aggregated percentiles retained per existing metrics policy.
Alert thresholds are intentionally conservative to reduce noise; we will iterate after an initial 2-week burn-in period.
We considered adding per-customer SLO heatmap here, but will scope to a follow-up (ENG-412359) to keep this ticket focused.
